summary: Master Outcome Harvesting techniques to identify and verify social change. Learn contribution analysis and substantiation in this 5-day expert-led course.
lede: Outcome harvesting training helps monitoring and evaluation professionals trace observable changes back to an intervention’s contribution. Designed for practitioners working in complex settings, it covers harvest design, identifying behavioral or policy change signals, drafting verifiable outcome descriptions, and substantiating findings. Participants also practice analyzing contribution, alternative explanations, and patterns across qualitative evidence to inform reporting and adaptive management.
audienceIntro: This intermediate-level course is ideal for professionals who already possess a foundational understanding of monitoring and evaluation but need more sophisticated tools for complex environments.
audience: Learning and Knowledge Managers focused on adaptive
modules: Foundations of Outcome Harvesting and Complexity
Identifying Outcome Signals and Data Extraction
Qualitative Data Analysis and Pattern Finding
prerequisites: Participants should have at least 2 years of experience in Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) or program management. Familiarity with basic Theory of Change (ToC) concepts and qualitative research methods is highly recommended. No prior experience with Outcome Harvesting is required, but a working knowledge of international development or social impact frameworks is beneficial.
